{"task": {"id": "I_kwDOVRkquM8AAAABbacDIw", "item_id": "PVTI_lAHOAHSLSM4Bn_T5zhE-_fs", "project_id": "PVT_kwHOAHSLSM4Bn_T5", "number": 128, "title": "Clarify cartridge insertion prompts and make Reset restart playback", "body": "## Problem

The browser SNES emulator's cartridge wording and Reset behavior are less intuitive than necessary:

1. The persistent cartridge-slot button says **"Change cartridge"**, including before any cartridge has been inserted.
2. The empty game screen says **"Ready when you are"**, which does not tell a new visitor what to do.
3. Clicking **Reset** calls `pause()`, then `core.reset()`, and leaves the emulator stopped. Users expect the console-style Reset button to restart the inserted game **and immediately continue playing**, without requiring a separate Play click.

Current baseline: `main` at `b6a62fec00b25871236d9b395d8add52ffd355d2`. See [web/index.html](https://github.com/takahirox/snes-rust/blob/main/web/index.html) (`#change-cartridge`, `#placeholder`, `#reset`) and [web/app.js](https://github.com/takahirox/snes-rust/blob/main/web/app.js) (Reset click handler, `pause()`, `start()`, `updatePlayback()`).

Keep the current stable cartridge-slot layout introduced in [Issue #122](https://github.com/takahirox/snes-rust/issues/122); this is a focused copy-and-interaction refinement, **not** a new design or different cartridge workflow.

## Expected outcome

- The persistent cartridge button reads **"Insert cartridge"** in all states, regardless of whether a game is already inserted. Its existing popover remains the single source selector, offering the two bundled games (**潮鳴りの密室** and **夜鳴き鐘**) and **Open local ROM…**.
- Before the first cartridge is loaded, the neutral screen placeholder reads **"Insert a cartridge"** instead of "Ready when you are". Once a valid ROM is inserted, the placeholder disappears as it does today. Keep the nearby **Inserted cartridge / None** field so the current state is unambiguous.
- Clicking **Reset** restarts the current ROM from reset, **preserves battery-backed SRAM**, and automatically starts or resumes emulation when permitted. It must work both while the game is currently playing and when it is paused; the common playback button should then correctly display **Pause**. Reset is for restarting; **Play/Pause** alone controls manual pausing.
- Retain the *same screen, cartridge slot and toolbar geometry* before and after insertion and after reset; no new redundant buttons or explanatory paragraphs.

Follow the [README UI/UX principles](https://github.com/takahirox/snes-rust/blob/main/README.md#uiux): **Keep it simple; Show, don't tell; Intuitive and predictable**.

## Context and implementation details

- Preserve the existing `#change-cartridge` id, popover target, file picker and accessible semantics where practical. Change user-visible copy and any matching documentation, test expectations and accessible labels without reworking the menu. **Insert cartridge** is an action available even when one is already inserted; its meaning is to choose the cartridge in the slot.
- The placeholder is shown only before a cartridge is loaded. Do not put the instruction over a running game or allow it to obscure error/recovery messages.
- Use the existing `start()` and playback-state update machinery after `core.reset()` rather than inventing a second playback implementation. Stop and discard old queued audio and held input appropriately, then resume video/audio scheduling without duplicate sources, lost input release or a stale frame. An explicit Reset click is a user gesture: attempt audio activation if needed, but **do not prevent video/gameplay from running when Web Audio is unavailable**.
- Preserve existing safety: do not reset an absent cartridge, while a ROM change is in flight or while save restoration is unresolved. Keep SRAM intact; keep meaningful persistence/restore failure warnings and do not overwrite existing recoverable saves. A failed core reset must report an error rather than claim playback resumed.
- Respect existing hidden-tab behavior: do not secretly advance emulation when the document is hidden. When visible and Reset is allowed, the default post-reset state is **playing**, even if it was previously paused.
- Keep cartridge selection, automatic playback after choosing a bundled or local ROM, the one common Play/Pause control, native keyboard/gamepad and all 12 mobile touch buttons, portrait/landscape/fullscreen handling, Pages subpath, legally required notices and privacy protections unchanged.
- Do not change either bundled ROM binary, its SHA-256, SRAM identity, the Rust/Wasm hardware implementation or the published static artifact allowlist.

## Pre-merge acceptance

- [ ] In a fresh desktop and mobile browser session, the UI displays **Insert cartridge** on the persistent selector and **Insert a cartridge** in the empty screen, with the adjacent **Inserted cartridge: None** value. No "Ready when you are" or "Change cartridge" remains in current user-facing UI/help.
- [ ] After inserting either bundled demo or a local ROM, the same **Insert cartridge** button and selector remain available in the same position, the inserted name updates, the placeholder disappears, and cartridge selection continues to autoplay successfully. Picker dismissal or file-choice cancellation still leaves the current game running.
- [ ] Using genuine Wasm/Chromium execution, **Reset while playing** returns the game to its reset state and subsequently advances frames/accepts input **without an extra Play click**. Playback status and the single toolbar button correctly reflect the playing state, with no duplicate pause control.
- [ ] **Reset while paused** also restarts and automatically plays. Reset remains disabled/guarded with no cartridge, during an in-flight load, and during unresolved SRAM restoration. Test the error branch if `core.reset()` fails; do not falsely show "Playing".
- [ ] Verify SRAM is preserved by reset (including battery-backed demo/local saves) and that save/persistence warnings and restore safeguards are not lost. Test that old audio buffers are flushed, new playback has bounded scheduling and sound-blocked browsers still play video with useful recovery feedback.
- [ ] Real Playwright tests cover the visible copy and reset behavior for desktop, narrow portrait and short landscape, and confirm no extra clicks or UI shifts, all twelve mobile buttons, keyboard/gamepad interaction, 256/512 canvas handling and no console/CSP/request errors. Update existing assertions meaningfully rather than deleting regression coverage.
- [ ] Keep the existing two bundled demos and legal notices intact. Pass the production Wasm/static build and relevant full browser suite, including Pages asset/subpath smoke checks; run repository's applicable Rust formatting, warning-denying Clippy, tests and licensed fixture gates, accurately reporting results, failures and optional skips. No emulator hardware change should be required.
- [ ] Document the concise behavioral change and test evidence in the PR or focused validation note. Avoid creating lengthy new user-visible explanatory copy or unnecessary dependencies.

## Optional validation

Physical iOS Safari/Android Chrome checks and qualitative first-time user feedback. These are useful but are not required for pre-merge acceptance when the browser tests pass.

## Required post-merge verification

After merging, the PR author/merger checks the **new main GitHub Pages deployment** and the live app on desktop and mobile viewports: new labels, stable cartridge selector, reset-to-playing from both playing and paused, video/input/audio behavior, and no 404/CSP/MIME/runtime errors. Record the workflow run/live URL and actual results. This can only occur after the merge and **must not block pre-merge approval**. On failure, create a separate `task` Issue with reproduction and evidence when invoked; do not imply automatic background monitoring.

## Related work

- [Issue #122](https://github.com/takahirox/snes-rust/issues/122): unified cartridge insertion/selection and autoplay, completed by PR #123.
- [Issue #126](https://github.com/takahirox/snes-rust/issues/126): second bundled demo.
- [Development flow](https://github.com/takahirox/snes-rust/blob/main/docs/development-flow.md): Issue → implementation → PR → review → merge.
